What do you get when you mix a small-town love triangle (or maybe square) with a sociopathic personality? A story that will make your jaw drop.

In Iron River, Michigan, the quiet life of Air Force veteran Chris Regan ended in a terrifying tragedy. The trail led police straight to Kelly and Jason Cochran, a married couple whose “open marriage” came with a deadly rule.

This case has it all:

A cheating scandal turned deadly

A desperate hunt for a missing body

A twisted marriage “pact” that led to murder

And shocking allegations from neighbors who believe they were unknowingly served human meat at a backyard barbecue

Kelly Cochran’s lies, games, and shocking admissions left investigators and the public wondering—was she a cold-blooded killer, or something even darker?

Join me as we dive into one of the most disturbing true crime cases of recent years.

Bailey you should do a podcast on GM and the Big Three because it’s not just about cars, it’s about power, community, and the collapse of entire towns that once thrived. Detroit, Pontiac, and Flint were built on the promise of steady work, strong unions, and middle-class stability. Generations of families gave their lives to the assembly lines, fueling not just the auto industry, but the global economy.

Yet, when corporate priorities shifted outsourcing, automation, profit over people these towns were abandoned. GM and the Big Three took their tax breaks, subsidies, and political power, but when it came time to reinvest in the communities that built them, they left. Plants shuttered, jobs disappeared, and the ripple effects devastated schools, neighborhoods, and local economies. What’s left are hollowed-out cities struggling with poverty, crime, and infrastructure collapse. Flint’s water crisis, Detroit’s bankruptcy, Pontiac’s empty factories these aren’t isolated tragedies, they’re symptoms of corporate abandonment.

A podcast on this wouldn’t just be a history lesson. It would be a story of accountability. Of how decisions in boardrooms shaped the destiny of entire cities. Of resilience in communities left behind. And of the lessons America still hasn’t learned about what happens when we let corporations grow at the expense of people.

Detroit, Pontiac, and Flint aren’t just backdrops they’re living case studies of what happens when industry builds up a town, then walks away. Your voice could give these stories the depth, honesty, and urgency they deserve.

As someone who was formerly a Pontiac resident, I witnessed this collapse firsthand. My grandfather was directly impacted by the downfall, and I grew up watching communities crumble as a result.
